entries.title: Iran releases footage of missiles launched at Israel
entries.snippet: Iran said its attacks were "the beginning of a full week of continuous strikes."

entries.title: At least 32 dead after major earthquake strikes southern Philippines
entries.snippet: The magnitude-7.8 quake triggered small tsunami waves in the Philippines, Indonesia and Japan.

entries.title: Armenia's pro-West government wins election despite Russian pressure
entries.snippet: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan's Civil Contract Party secures nearly 50% of the vote, comfortably beating the other contenders.

entries.title: 'A World Cup for them not us': Fans' anger at US travel bans and visa restrictions
entries.snippet: Fans across the world say US travel bans and visa regulations make them feel excluded from the World Cup.

entries.title: Knicks' long-awaited NBA run electrifies NYC, with Trump set to attend key game
entries.snippet: The Knicks' stunning winning streak has energised the city as the New York basketball team prepares for the third game of the finals series at its home arena.

entries.title: Rare footage captured of Great White shark in Mediterranean Sea
entries.snippet: A volunteer diver has described shaking as he filmed his encounter with an endangered Great White shark between Tunisia and Sicily.

entries.title: Malawians repatriated from South Africa amid xenophobia concerns
entries.snippet: Malawi is among several African nations transporting their citizens out of the country following reports of violence against migrants.

entries.title: Stock markets fall on tech plunge and renewed Middle East attacks
entries.snippet: Markets in Europe and Asia were hit by a tech sell-off, and oil rises as Iran and Israel launch attacks on each other.

entries.title: Zelensky's close European allies set out five conditions for peace talks
entries.snippet: The Ukrainian president's meeting with his staunchest European allies came as US President Donald Trump's focus shifts to the war with Iran.

entries.title: Peru election result close as vote counting continues
entries.snippet: The race between right-wing Keiko Fujimori and left-wing Roberto Sánchez has been dominated by concerns over crime and political instability.

entries.title: Hundreds of captives freed from Boko Haram mountain hideout
entries.snippet: The group includes many women and children who were abducted in March from an area close to Cameroon.

entries.title: Trump abruptly ends NBC interview after clash over 'rigged election' claim
entries.snippet: During the interview, the president was repeatedly challenged on several points by the show's presenter Kristen Welker.

entries.title: Mexico City attempts record-breaking wave
entries.snippet: As part of the countdown to the World Cup, Mexico City is attempting to surpass the world record for largest wave.

entries.title: Insecurity and instability drive voters in Peru's tight presidential race
entries.snippet: After eight presidents in 10 years, many voters are looking for stability so the next president can focus on tackling crime and inequality.

entries.title: Eriksen conscious after collapsing in Denmark game
entries.snippet: Christian Eriksen collapsed during Denmark's friendly against Ukraine but is now conscious, says the Danish Football Association.

entries.title: Friendship or leverage: Why is Xi Jinping in North Korea?
entries.snippet: Beijing is trying to reassert influence over a strategically vital yet deeply unpredictable partner.

entries.title: 'We don't look at the sky anymore': The Air India crash victims who were not on the plane
entries.snippet: A grandfather, a survivor, a witness: one year after the crash, the people on the ground tell their stories.

entries.title: Spain's visitor numbers hit new highs as tourists avoid Middle East
entries.snippet: The European country had 9.1 million international visitors in April, the most ever for that month.

entries.title: 'No dead ends': What the Dutch can teach us about tackling youth unemployment
entries.snippet: The Netherlands has one of the world's lowest rates of 16 to 24-year-olds not in education, employment or training.

entries.title: Steve Rosenberg: Russia's economic forum overshadowed by drone attacks on St Petersburg
entries.snippet: The BBC's Russia editor saw Putin's flagship economic event overshadowed by Ukrainian drones attacks.

entries.title: Xi and Kim express hopes for greater ties between China and North Korea
entries.snippet: Xi traveled to Pyongyang on Monday in a likely attempt to reassert China's unique influence over its socialist neighbor.

entries.title: Israel-Iran strikes threaten truce. And, Ebola is spreading at an unprecedented rate
entries.snippet: Israel and Iran's recent exchange of fire is threatening the truce in the Middle East. And, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is spreading at an unprecedented rate, officials say.

entries.title: In his book, self-described USAID 'whistleblower' talks about the agency and Ebola
entries.snippet: Nicholas Enrich, on staff at the U.S. Agency for International Aid under 4 administrations, talks about Into the Woodchipper: A Whistleblower's Account of How the Trump Administration Shredded USAID.

entries.title: In speech to Spanish parliament, pope demands respect for the dignity of all people
entries.snippet: In the first papal address to the Spanish legislature, the American pope said a "moral renewal" was necessary in legislatures and public life to ensure respect for the inherent dignity of all people.

entries.title: The red state, blue state divide is real. But it's driven by more than just politics
entries.snippet: Recent research suggests there's more going on with "ideological sorting" than simply moving to places that match one's politics. It's often one of many deciding factors, such as taxes or safety.

entries.title: People love working from home. But does it love them back? A new study says no
entries.snippet: A study finds that people in remote jobs are more socially isolated, anxious and sad compared to people not in remote jobs. But demanding everyone return to the office isn't the answer either, say researchers.

entries.title: Can a vibrating belt fend off bone density loss?
entries.snippet: More than 40 million adults in the U.S. aged 50 and older have osteopenia, or low bone density. An FDA-approved wearable vibration device is giving some women a tool that could slow that loss.

entries.title: Whales are showing up in San Francisco Bay. New ship alerts could help protect them
entries.snippet: The changing climate is driving whales into San Francisco Bay, where ship strikes have been deadly. A new camera system could help ships and ferries steer clear.

entries.title: Morning news brief
entries.snippet: Israel and Iran traded fire early Monday in retaliatory strikes, Trump walked out of an interview after being pressed on election fraud claims, ebola outbreak is spreading at alarming rate.

entries.title: Israel and Iran exchange missile fire threatening Middle East truce
entries.snippet: The exchange marked a major escalation in the already tense region. It came on the 100th day of a war that began on Feb. 28, further complicating efforts to end Middle East fighting.

entries.title: European leaders stress 'urgent need' to bolster Ukraine's defenses against Russian ballistic missiles
entries.snippet: The leaders of the U.K., Ukraine, France and Germany discussed the "urgent need" to ramp up production of weapons to combat Russia's powerful hypersonic Oreshnik ballistic missiles in a meeting in London on Sunday.

entries.title: Palestinian man with Israeli citizenship opens fire in central Israel, killing 1 and wounding 5
entries.snippet: A Palestinian man with Israeli citizenship went on a shooting rampage in several towns in central Israel on Sunday, killing a reservist and wounding five other people, according to Israeli police and the military.

entries.title: Israel says Iran launched missiles in first bombardment since fragile ceasefire
entries.snippet: Iran launched missiles at Israel in the first such bombardment since a fragile ceasefire took effect in early April, raising the possibility of a return to heavy fighting and complicating mediation efforts to end the war.

entries.title: Kimi Antonelli wins Monaco Grand Prix, sets record as youngest winner in race history
entries.snippet: Antonelli was on course for victory with 10 laps remaining when the race was red-flagged after parts of the asphalt broke away and two cars crashed in quick succession.

entries.title: Lawsuit aims to block UFC fight on White House South Lawn for Trump's birthday
entries.snippet: A federal lawsuit seeks to halt the upcoming UFC fight card on the White House South Lawn in a mixed martial arts show timed for President Donald Trump's 80th birthday and the nation's 250th anniversary.

entries.title: Alexander Zverev wins French Open for first Grand Slam title
entries.snippet: In his fourth major final, Zverev beat Flavio Cobolli 6-1, 4-6, 6-4, 6-7 (5), 6-1 for the French Open title on Sunday.

entries.title: Initial results show Kurti's party wins most votes in Kosovo's early election
entries.snippet: Prime Minister Albin Kurti's party won the most votes in an early parliamentary election in Kosovo on Sunday, early results showed.

entries.title: Health workers at center of Congo's Ebola outbreak labor with little pay or rest
entries.snippet: Health workers are handling the disease with minimal resources, because agencies have been scrambling to bring aid into the region.

entries.title: Trump to attend Knicks' NBA Finals game in New York
entries.snippet: Invited by Knicks owner James Dolan, he will be the first sitting president to attend an NBA Finals game.

entries.title: Police seek suspects in Ohio shooting that wounded 12 near street festival
entries.snippet: A search in Ohio for suspects who opened fire near a busy street festival stretched into Sunday after 12 people were wounded in the weekend shooting that sent crowds scrambling for cover in a historic Toledo neighborhood.

entries.title: Nigerian army frees 360 people abducted by Boko Haram
entries.snippet: The Nigerian army said Sunday it freed 360 people abducted by Boko Haram in southern Borno, in the northeastern part of the country.

entries.title: Multiple people shot near festival in Toledo, Ohio, authorities say
entries.snippet: Multiple people were shot Saturday afternoon near a community street festival in Toledo, Ohio, police said.

entries.title: What to know about the protests and arrests outside a New Jersey detention center
entries.snippet: Clashes between demonstrators and law enforcement outside a New Jersey immigration detention center since late May have become the latest flashpoint for protests against President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown.

entries.title: What's next for the War Powers Resolution on Iran? PolitiFact explains
entries.snippet: The House and Senate have advanced war powers resolutions aimed at curbing President Donald Trump from continuing the war in Iran. Can a 53-year-old law make a difference? What steps would be required to end the war? PolitiFact explains.

entries.title: Former first lady of France Bernadette Chirac dies at 93
entries.snippet: Bernadette Chirac, the steel-willed former first lady of France who spent 12 years at the Élysée Palace from 1995 to 2007 beside President Jacques Chirac, has died at 93.

entries.title: U.S. mortgage rates are staying high – and the Federal Reserve can do little about it
entries.snippet: Investors' inflation expectations, much more than the central bank, are among the factors that affect the cost of home loans.

entries.title: Pope Leo XIV warns against 'fanning the flames of polarization' on first papal visit to Spain in 15 years
entries.snippet: Pope Leo XIV urged Spaniards on Saturday to stop "fanning the flames of polarization" as he arrived in Spain at a moment of political turmoil for the Socialist-led government and a credibility crisis for the Catholic Church.

entries.title: U.S.-Iran exchange of fire in Gulf tests fragile ceasefire
entries.snippet: Iran fired ballistic missiles and drones toward Bahrain and Kuwait that were intercepted early Saturday, Bahrain's government said, and called on Tehran to halt attacks on Gulf neighbors that test a fragile ceasefire in the Middle East conflict.

entries.title: Hegseth warns of 'invasion' and 'dangerous ideologies' in D-Day anniversary speech
entries.snippet: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth used a D-Day anniversary speech on Saturday to appear to link immigration by sea to the wartime liberation of Europe, warning that the freedom won by Allied troops could prove temporary if leaders failed to defend it.

entries.title: Trump pardons former Republican congressman convicted of insider trading
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump has issued a pardon to Stephen Buyer, a former Republican congressman from Indiana who served nearly two years in prison for making illegal stock trades based on inside information after he left office.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: China's Xi begins rare North Korea visit
entries.snippet: China's President Xi Jinping has kicked off his first visit to North Korea in seven years. It is also Xi's first international trip this year after hosting key summits with US and Russian leaders.

entries.title: Teacher protests in Mexico could spoil the World Cup party
entries.snippet: Just before the opening of the World Cup, host country Mexico faces a political tug-of-war. Striking teachers have occupied the central fan zone and have pledged to continue protesting.

entries.title: Depression in romantic relationships: You, me and the illness
entries.snippet: Depression can be a huge challenge for a relationship. Loved ones of someone with depression often feel helpless. But there is actually a lot they can do ― and a lot they shouldn't.

entries.title: Peru: Presidential election too close to call
entries.snippet: With over 90% of the votes counted in Peru's runoff presidential election, right-wing conservative candidate Keiko Fujimori and left-wing politician Roberto Sanchez are in a neck-and-neck race.

entries.title: Latvia: NATO jet shoots down stray drone
entries.snippet: For the first time, a NATO jet shot down a drone over eastern Latvia. According to the military, the drone entered Latvian airspace due to "Russian electromagnetic warfare."

entries.title: Germany news: Arson suspected in large-scale power outage
entries.snippet: Around 10,000 households in the southwestern city of Reutlingen have been affected by the outage, which is reminiscent of recent far-left arson attacks in Berlin. DW has more.

entries.title: What is wrong with the 2026 World Cup
entries.snippet: The 2026 World Cup has come under fire even before kickoff. Criticism is mounting over US President Donald Trump’s politics, high ticket prices, the expansion to 48 teams as well as its environmental impact.

entries.title: Jafar Panahi's prison sentence confirmed by Iranian court
entries.snippet: Following a retrial for a verdict that had been reached while the prominent Iranian director was abroad, the Revolutionary Court in Tehran has upheld a one-year jail sentence.

entries.title: Armenia election: Prime Minister Pashinyan declares victory
entries.snippet: The election result cements Nikol Pashinyan's Westward push away from Russian influence. It is the first vote since a 2023 crushing military defeat by Azerbaijan.

entries.title: Indian stock markets dive amid Middle East escalation
entries.snippet: India's Sensex and Nifty have fallen over 13% and 10% in 2026, hurting retail investors. Monday's stock losses only add to that pain. Meanwhile, Kerala is in danger of landslides amid monsoon showers. Follow live.

entries.title: Philippines lifts tsunami alert after deadly 7.8 earthquake
entries.snippet: The Philippines and Indonesia both issued tsunami warnings after a powerful 7.8 magnitude earthquake struck off Mindanao. At least 32 people were killed and more than 200 injured.

entries.title: UK, Germany, France back ceasefire talks between Ukraine and Russia
entries.snippet: The British, German and French leaders backed a call by Ukraine's Zelenskyy for direct talks with Russian President Putin. The European leaders met Zelenskyy in London.

entries.title: Middle East updates: Iran declares end to attacks on Israel
entries.snippet: Iran's military said it would halt its operations against Israel, but warned that strikes would resume if Israel attacked Lebanon. The announcement came after Trump called for an end to the fighting. Follow DW for more.

entries.title: Kosovo PM wins snap vote, but with no majority
entries.snippet: Sunday's vote, the country's third in just over a year, was marked by low turnout. The country's prolonged political crisis has further debilitated an already ailing economy.

entries.title: SIPRI: With peace elusive, nuclear weapons make a comeback
entries.snippet: Governments are increasingly turning to nuclear deterrence. As the global arms buildup intensifies, so do the risks, the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute warns.

entries.title: Zelenskyy angers Poland with WWII-era name for army unit
entries.snippet: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has sparked outrage in Poland by choosing a name that carries Nazi connotations for a Ukrainian army unit. Can Polish PM Donald Tusk smooth things over?

entries.title: Reports: Iran uses war as cover for increased executions
entries.snippet: Iran already had one of the highest rates of capital punishment in the world. Now, rights groups say, the country is using the current conflict to carry out even more executions, in an attempt to repress dissent.

entries.title: French Open: Germany's Zverev wins first ever Grand Slam after defeating Italy's Cobolli
entries.snippet: Alexander Zverev has won his first Grand Slam title at the fourth attempt, beating Flavio Cobolli in a five-set epic in Paris. He is the first German man to win a major singles title in 30 years.

entries.title: German political rivals revive 'pizza connection'
entries.snippet: An unusual forum for exchange between German conservative and Greens politicians emerged 30 years ago in the form of the "pizza connection." Now that format is being revived in a changed political landscape.
